Relationships and flows

Source: vignettes/articles/relationships.Rmd
relationships.Rmd

Charts for the relationship between two numeric variables, and for flows between categories.

Chart Use it when
scatter_plot() You look at the relationship between two numeric variables
hexbin_plot() A scatter plot has too many points to read
chord_diagram() You show flows between categories, such as migration or trade

scatter_plot()

Let’s work with the mpg data frame from the ggplot2 package.

library(ggplot2) # needed for the mpg data frame

scatter_plot(
  data = mpg,
  x = "hwy",
  y = "cty",
  xtitle = "hwy variable",
  ytitle = "cty variable",
  title = "cty and hwy relationship",
  titleFontSize = 20
)

In comparison to ggplot2, graphics’ customization in ddplot is limited nonetheless you get a fully vectorized SVG which is cool.

scatter_plot(
  data = mpg,
  x = "displ",
  y = "cty",
  col = "tomato",
  bgcol = "pink",
  size = 3,
  stroke = "royalblue",
  strokeWidth = 1,
  xtitle = "displ variable",
  ytitle = "cty variable",
  xticks = 3,
  yticks = 3)

hexbin_plot()

hexbin_plot() is inspired by the hexbin transform of Observable Plot. It groups points into a grid of hexagons coloured by the number of observations in each one, which keeps dense scatter plots readable. The binning is written by hand, since d3-hexbin is not bundled with r2d3.

hexbin_plot(
  data     = faithful,
  x        = "waiting",
  y        = "eruptions",
  binWidth = 14,
  xtitle   = "Waiting time to next eruption (min)",
  ytitle   = "Eruption duration (min)",
  title    = "Old Faithful eruptions"
)

A log colour scale helps when counts are very skewed:

set.seed(1)
dsample <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 10000), ]

hexbin_plot(
  data         = dsample,
  x            = "carat",
  y            = "price",
  binWidth     = 8,
  colorPalette = "Viridis",
  colorScale   = "log",
  title        = "Diamond price by carat"
)

chord_diagram()

chord_diagram() shows the flows between a set of entities as outer arcs joined by ribbons. Its look and hover behaviour are inspired by the chord chart of Nivo: hovering over an entity fades every ribbon not connected to it, and clicking an arc pins the highlight.

migration <- data.frame(
  from  = c("Africa", "Africa", "Africa", "Asia", "Asia", "Asia",
            "Europe", "Europe", "Latin America", "Latin America",
            "North America", "Oceania", "Asia", "Europe"),
  to    = c("Europe", "North America", "Asia", "Europe", "North America",
            "Oceania", "North America", "Asia", "North America", "Europe",
            "Europe", "Asia", "Africa", "Oceania"),
  value = c(420, 150, 90, 610, 520, 230, 180, 120, 870, 260,
            95, 40, 60, 75)
)

chord_diagram(
  data        = migration,
  from        = "from",
  to          = "to",
  value       = "value",
  valueFormat = ",.0f",
  title       = "Migration flows between regions (illustrative data)"
)

A square matrix with dimnames works too:

hair <- matrix(
  c(11975,  5871, 8916, 2868,
     1951, 10048, 2060, 6171,
     8010, 16145, 8090, 8045,
     1013,   990,  940, 6907),
  nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(c("Black", "Blond", "Brown", "Red"),
                  c("Black", "Blond", "Brown", "Red"))
)

chord_diagram(
  data        = hair,
  colors      = c("#3b3b3b", "#f2c45a", "#8c5a3c", "#d0533a"),
  ribbonColor = "gradient",
  padAngle    = 0.05,
  valueFormat = ",.0f",
  title       = "Hair color flows"
)
